spatial_rubric.zone: Must-hit keywords: upper-left quadrant, lower-right quadrant, central area, wafer center. A correct answer should state that the main defect crosses near the wafer center and extends diagonally across the wafer.
spatial_rubric.distribution: Must-hit keywords: diagonal, linear, band or trace, dominant feature, sparse isolated defects elsewhere. The distribution is a prominent diagonal defect band from upper-left toward lower-right with only small scattered defects outside the main line.
spatial_rubric.clock_position: Must-hit keywords: upper-left to lower-right. Acceptable clock-position phrasing: approximately 10 o'clock/10:30 toward 4 o'clock/4:30, crossing center.
spatial_rubric.coordinates_hint: Must-hit keywords: diagonal from negative-x/positive-y region toward positive-x/negative-y region, near center, central crossing. Coordinate references should describe an upper-left to lower-right trajectory through the wafer center.

morphology_rubric.pattern_type: Must-hit keywords: scratch-like, continuous line, diagonal line, jagged, segmented or slightly segmented. The main morphology is a narrow scratch trace rather than a broad area defect.
morphology_rubric.density: Must-hit keywords: dominant main line, sparse background speckles, isolated defects elsewhere, low-density background. The scratch itself is prominent while other defects are sparse.
morphology_rubric.geometric_structure: Must-hit keywords: narrow width, linear, diagonal, elongated, irregular. The geometry should be described as a thin elongated defect crossing the central wafer area.
morphology_rubric.texture_description: Must-hit keywords: bright, jagged, irregular intensity, slightly segmented, stands out from background speckles. The scratch has uneven brightness and a broken/segmented appearance but remains essentially continuous.

summary: A dominant bright, narrow, jagged diagonal scratch runs from the upper-left quadrant to the lower-right quadrant, crossing near the wafer center, with sparse isolated background defects elsewhere.
